profile.beat: A research-shop account (Jag, with paying European clients and a website) posting on US equity breadth, rates and geopolitics, plus a concentrated growth book led by META, the cybersecurity ETF BUG and RKLB, with space and speculative disruptor names on the side.
profile.style: Bold, promotional conviction language on core holdings ('You are still not bullish enough', 'a trillion dollar company in the making') set against a bearish macro and breadth tape read. Discloses top positions openly. Mostly one-line 'Bullish for $X' reactions to news rather than worked fundamental cases in-feed; deeper reports sit behind links to its own paid research.
profile.cadence: Several posts a day: short originals with charts, quote posts reacting to headlines, and many off-topic or joking replies. Recurring themes are market breadth deterioration, the 10-year yield, and the Houthi/Saudi conflict. Mentions a recurring weekend 'Convexity' trade (seventh in seven weeks).
profile.caveats: The account sells research to clients and promotes teaser reports with undisclosed tickers (2102553954999742475, 2102797205719363645), so bullish calls double as marketing. Top-position disclosures mean it talks its own book. A large share of posts are political or off-topic banter. Macro stance (bearish breadth, rising yields) sits in tension with a very aggressive long growth book, and risk is rarely addressed on single names.

narrative: Across the window the account ran two tracks. On macro, it was consistently bearish on internals: terrible breadth, half the S&P below its 200-day while the index held up, many sector ETFs breaking down, and a K-shaped economy where crude, yields and the dollar rise while the Russell falls, which it tied to the ongoing Middle East war. By the end of the window it was pointing at the US 10-year yield rising daily and questioning why markets pretend this does not matter for consumers and businesses. On the book, it stayed aggressively long its top three positions, META, BUG and RKLB, calling META far from fully appreciated and RKLB a future trillion-dollar company that weak hands will sell. It added a conditional long on Petrobras/Brazil tied to the October Brazilian election outcome and flagged Planet Labs as bullish on a Google-linked program. It also teased an unnamed speculative disruptor report and an 'agentic economy' underwriter report for clients. There was no visible change of view during the week; the bearish macro read and bullish growth-book stance ran in parallel.
